purpose: Close the shared runtime output redaction result for application logs and safe API errors without turning the sanitizer into product authority.
success_outcome: Actual current runtime log/settings summaries and API error serialization remove the configured secret/auth corpus before output, never mutate source credentials, and fail safely without echoing rejected values.
anti_goals: Do not redesign every product payload, add logging infrastructure, persist redaction state, or weaken stable error catalogs.
Do not adopt manifest, Timeline/history, Bus/UI, or agent-context ACs owned by sibling tasks.
constraints: Use one configured secret corpus and actual serializers, not pattern-only unit assertions.
Sanitize output copies before emission; authentication/provider source values remain unchanged.
invariants: No runtime log or safe API error contains the forbidden corpus.
Sanitization grants no runtime, audit, UI, agent, upload, or sync authority.
verification_targets: FT-015-AC-003: actual log/error RED/GREEN or preserved pre-GREEN with corpus absence, safe failure, and source-value integrity.
Full deterministic backend regression after any shared sanitizer change.

forbidden_scope: Manifest, Timeline/history, Bus/UI, provider-request semantics, database schema, frontend, and historical evidence.
stop_conditions: A fix requires changing a public error code/shape or credential lifecycle.
One shared primitive cannot be changed without an unresolved incompatible consumer contract.
